children.value: Terrain is a reproducible observatory over the transit model stack. The four-step model computes server-side; Terrain catalogs the models, steps, datasets and layers as editable rows and traces every published number back to its model version, input datasets, soundness checks and confidence tier.
What is real

Real now: composed views, CSV imports, and the full reproducibility trail. Phase 2 (needs engine): drag-resize panes and a native map that paints your own layers and shows, for the coordinates on screen, the proof-chain from raw source through each pipeline stage to the delivered value. Phase 3 (needs server): live model, custom-zone and GTFS jobs once the /model endpoint authorizes the app.
Confidence tiers

Focused (green) = calibrated to real sourced local targets, residuals within tolerance, cross-checked. Exploratory (amber) = national or peer anchors — directionally useful, not a calibrated forecast. Promotion is earned by sourced targets and in-tolerance calibration, never by editing the label.
Model runs, honestly

As of 2026-07-06 every /model/* route answers HTTP 403 — locked at the edge since the token lockdown. ▶ Run scenario therefore records the run locally with a full snapshot of the setup (model version, tier, β, transit_calib, calibration method, zone system, city, year, growth, note). The live call is wired (same chain as Atlas) and degrades silently; the day the edge authorizes this app, the same tap also lands a second row labeled 'live model run' with the server's numbers — the pair shares its launch stamp. β, transit_calib and growth are RECORDED on the run, not sent: today's engine cannot attach table values to request bodies, so the live call carries the year only. Web builds additionally need CORS on /model/*. Only the four-step engine is runnable; the other layers read its outputs. Endpoint swap point: the six http blocks on the Runs screen + app.json meta.
Suite roles

Terrain's Runs is the cockpit ledger: launches you record here plus curated real run reports. The Scenarios applet remains the deep-provenance archive (run inputs, checks, history); Atlas maps outputs; Model reports charts them.
Seeded history

Past runs are real transit4 run reports generated 2026-07-01; each row's status names its source file. Exploratory rows hit their targets exactly because targets are transferred anchors; NY/London trip lengths are geometry-limited (β at floor) and carry their real warnings; Boston appears at two resolutions because β honestly moves with zone size (0.0579 at TAZ → 0.1271 at block group). One benign stamp mismatch is preserved, not smoothed: run reports stamp foundation fee6a0b while the changelog stamps f35456f.
Standards conformance
Standards: FHWA / NCHRP-716 / TMIP / STOPS — pinned per model on the model record.
A defensible model shows its methodology, its cited inputs, its calibration residuals, its re-runnable versions, and its stated limits — Terrain surfaces all five as rows you can inspect.
One universal model, regional settings

There is one baseline engine — the same four-step model everywhere — never a different model per place. Each region gets settings, not a fork: calibrated β and transit share against sourced local targets, with urban, suburban and rural treated as distinct travel-behavior contexts (suburban deliberately not lumped into either).
One data format

Every table in this suite is the same standardized, transportable data object used across all applets — one format for import, export, snapshot, backup, sync and sharing, so a slice you save here opens anywhere.
Safe change practices

Changes ship additive-only through a schema-compatibility gate; every run pins a model version (git sha); raw sources are never edited in place; and nightly integrity-checked backups are restore-verified. Future-proofing is built into the pipeline, not promised.

Model-card facts (calibration, sources, extents) are curated summaries of the registries — when a registry row changes, update the model card in the same edit. On module lists, a teal stripe marks a swappable component.
